subject: Jimmy Gomez
title: Jimmy Gomez resigns: Why is he leaving Congress? An ethics report
answer: Rep. Jimmy Gomez, a Los Angeles Democrat, said on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, that he will resign from Congress effective Dec. 1. He announced it the same day the House Ethics Committee released a report saying it found substantial evidence that he made unwanted sexual advances toward a House staffer in 2024.
in_the_news: Gomez is the third House member to resign over sexual misconduct findings or allegations in 2026, after Eric Swalwell and Tony Gonzales in April. He had already lost his November re-election race, so the resignation ends his term about a month early.
body:
The bipartisan Ethics Committee concluded that Gomez's behavior broke House rules and that he failed to grasp the power gap between lawmakers and staff, according to the Los Angeles Times and NBC News. The report describes two encounters with the same staffer in 2024, one at a Washington bar and one in his Capitol Hill office. The panel wrote that the conduct could amount to a misdemeanor under District of Columbia law. No criminal charges have been filed. The committee did not ask the full House to censure or expel him, which NBC News said was presumably because he was leaving in January anyway.

Gomez disputes the findings. In his statement he said he has "strong disagreements" with the report, argued that it leaves out key parts of his testimony, and said he takes full responsibility for "personal mistakes" outside his marriage. He has previously said his actions did not break the law or House rules. Attorneys for the former staffer praised the committee and called on Congress to fix what they described as a toxic workplace culture.

How the case unfolded: April 14, 2026 — Reps. Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.) and Tony Gonzales (R-Texas) resign on the same day, ahead of possible expulsion votes over misconduct allegations. Mid-April 2026 — a New York Post story says Gomez kissed a congressional aide at a party; he denies it. June 2026 — news reports say the Ethics Committee is investigating him. Aug. 17, 2026 — the committee publicly confirms its inquiry; days later, the former staffer's lawyers publicly allege sexual assault; Gomez has said his actions were consensual. Nov. 3, 2026 — Gomez loses his seat to fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres by nearly 25 points, the Los Angeles Times reported. Nov. 23, 2026 — the report comes out and he announces his resignation.

What happens next: Gomez's office is closing out constituent cases before Dec. 1. California's 34th District, which covers parts of East and Central Los Angeles, will then have no member of the House until Gonzales-Torres is sworn in when the new Congress convenes on Jan. 3, 2027. Days before the report came out, the Ethics Committee adopted procedural changes that include publicly disclosing substantiated sexual misconduct findings, so similar reports are likely to become public faster.

faq.q: When does Jimmy Gomez's resignation take effect?
faq.a: Dec. 1, 2026, about a month before his term was set to end.

faq.q: Has Jimmy Gomez been charged with a crime?
faq.a: No. The Ethics Committee said the conduct could amount to a misdemeanor, but no charges have been filed.
Angela Gonzales-Torres, a Democrat who defeated him on Nov. 3, 2026. She takes office on Jan. 3, 2027.

faq.q: What district does Jimmy Gomez represent?
faq.a: California's 34th Congressional District in Los Angeles, which he has represented since 2017.
